name: bsnes-mercury (ASYNCIFY, three profiles)

asyncify.why: bsnes uses libco cooperative cothreads. In a plain single-threaded, non-ASYNCIFY WASM build retro_run never returns (the libco scheduler never yields back to JS), so the first frame hangs. Building with -s ASYNCIFY=1 lets retro_run unwind the Emscripten stack and RETURN to the browser event loop.
asyncify.libco_backend: Emscripten Fibers (libco/emscripten.c, added for the __EMSCRIPTEN__ target in libco/libco.c). ASYNCIFY alone is not enough because libco context-switches raw stacks ASYNCIFY does not know about; the Fibers backend (emscripten_fiber_*) makes cothread switches cooperate with ASYNCIFY.
asyncify.asyncify_stack_size_note: Reduced 1048576 -> 524288. This setting sizes ONLY the primary context's unwind buffer; each libco fiber carries its own 256 KB buffer (libco/emscripten.c). The primary context's async stack is shallow (retro_run -> System::run -> scheduler -> co_switch), so 1 MiB was far more than needed. A 256 KiB build was verified across 300 frames; 512 KiB ships to keep a 2x margin.
asyncify.instrumented_functions_note: Ground truth from -s ASYNCIFY_ADVISE=1. 994 of the 1212 (82%) are instrumented only because they contain INDIRECT calls. That is NOT prunable here: bsnes reaches its fiber swap THROUGH indirect calls (Processor::R65816::op_* dispatch virtually to SuperFamicom::CPU::op_read, which calls co_switch; the whole bus map is nall::function<> lambdas). See asyncify_pruning_rejected in build.json.

fiber_swaps_per_frame.note: Measured with a -DLIBCO_SWAP_COUNTER diagnostic build (guarded, off by default; the shipped cores are byte-identical without it). This is the reason the accuracy profile is slow, and it is NOT a codegen problem: at ~1.15 us per Asyncify unwind+rewind, ~39.4k swaps/frame consume essentially the whole 45 ms frame. 60 FPS would require ~0.4 us/swap, which Asyncify cannot deliver. Fewer swaps (balanced/performance) is the only lever available; JSPI would give VM-native stack switching but iOS Safari does not support it.

optimization.defect_fixed: The Emscripten LINK step was running at its -O0 default. The generic Makefile block (`ifeq ($(DEBUG),0) FLAGS += -O3`) did put -O3 on CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS, so per-TU clang optimization was already on — but LDFLAGS is assembled as `LDFLAGS += $(fpic) $(SHARED)` and never receives $(FLAGS). Under Emscripten the link is not a formality: it runs wasm-opt over the whole module and it is where the ASYNCIFY instrumentation pass executes. At -O0 wasm-opt is skipped entirely, ASSERTIONS defaults to 1, and the JS glue is never minified.
compile_flags_added: -O3 (was already present via the generic DEBUG=0 block)
optimization.lto: NOT USED — measured and rejected. -flto (full): 2,084,760 B wasm and 47.1 ms/frame (13% bigger, 35% SLOWER than no-LTO's 34.9). -flto=thin: 2,056,177 B and 35.4 ms/frame (12% bigger, no speed gain). Both linked cleanly; both lost on measurement.
optimization.debug_symbols: None. No -g, no -gsource-map, no -sDEMANGLE_SUPPORT anywhere in the compile or link line.

accuracy.role: Reference profile for paused, frame-perfect sub-pixel TAS work. Renders the PPU dot-by-dot. Will NOT reach 60 FPS on-device — see asyncify.fiber_swaps_per_frame.
accuracy.verified: run-smoke 300 frames: retro_load_game true, retro_run returns (no hang), video_refresh non-null (512x224 XRGB8888), frame counter advances. ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED.

balanced.role: NEW. Still bsnes-derived (cycle-accurate CPU/SMP/DSP, scanline-granular PPU), so far more accurate than snes9x, but 7.5x cheaper per frame than the accuracy profile and therefore the realistic choice for near-60-FPS bsnes work on-device.
balanced.verified: run-smoke 300 frames: retro_load_game true, retro_run returns (no hang), video_refresh non-null (256x224 XRGB8888), frame counter advances. ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED.

performance.role: Fastest bsnes profile; relaxes the most timing fidelity.
performance.verified: run-smoke 300 frames: retro_load_game true, retro_run returns (no hang), video_refresh non-null (256x224 XRGB8888), frame counter advances. ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED.

output_note: Each profile is emitted with a DISTINCT filename AND a distinct MODULARIZE EXPORT_NAME (bsnes_accuracy / bsnes_balanced / bsnes_performance) so the cores never collide on a shared global/UMD symbol. All are emitted as ES6 modules (-s EXPORT_ES6=1), so core-loader.js resolves each via the dynamic-import default export. `--closure 1` was verified to preserve that `export default <EXPORT_NAME>` factory shape as well as ccall/cwrap/addFunction/HEAP* on the Module object.
emscripten_flags: -s EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS=[22 raw retro_* + _malloc + _free] (retro_cheat_set / retro_cheat_reset are NEVER exported)
